lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Hey, Juliet. Sorry, give me one second, I'm just getting my screen up.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: No rush. How's your day?

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Good, actually. I've been playing with the queue all morning. But you first. How was Ducal?

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Really good. Paris was great, very clear about what he needs. He asked for three things.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Okay, go.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: One, inspections that sync on their own when the tablet comes back online. Their yards have basically no signal past the first few rows of trailers. Two, a signed PDF for every inspection, because their auditors need a signed report within twenty-four hours. And three, export into their freight system, by site. They've got thirty sites.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Okay. So the first one is literally the queue.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: That's what I was hoping you'd say.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: The PDF is all you, that's Balcony. And export by site, um, that's new. That's not this week.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: No, agreed. I told him I'd be straight with him on timing. Oh, and he asked whether Ducal would see your routing data. I said no, only what Ducal sends.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Good. Yes. That's right. Okay, can I show you the thing?

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Please.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: So this is the prototype on a test tablet. At about two I turned off the wifi and just started making inspections. Fake ones. Dock four, dock seven, a very damaged imaginary trailer.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Poor trailer.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: It's had a hard day. So you can see here, twelve inspections queued. That's an hour offline. Nothing crashed, nothing got lost. Now watch. I'm turning the wifi back on.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Okay...

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: And there it goes. Eleven, eight, four... zero. All twelve sent, in order, and they're showing up on the Mesh Routing side. Same timestamps they were signed with, not the time they arrived.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Oh, that's important. The auditors care about when it was signed.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Exactly. That was the whole point of keeping the signed time on the record.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: That's really nice, Romeo. Tybalt said this morning he's satisfied if it survives a week of airplane mode.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Ha. Okay. One hour down, a hundred and sixty-seven to go.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: So, the thing I really want to settle today. Field versioning. It's the one open question left from Monday, and I've got an empty owner line in the spec staring at me.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Yeah. I've been thinking about it. Can I propose something?

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Go for it.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: So there are really two layers. There's the inspection record itself. Site, inspector, photos, findings, signed time. That's yours, that's what Balcony knows about. And then there's the envelope around it, the routing stuff, where it's going, delivery, retries. That's ours.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: So Capulet owns the inspection record schema, Montague owns the routing envelope.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Right. But, and here's the part I care about, any change to either one needs both of us to approve it. Because if you rename a field, my side breaks, and if I change the envelope, your side breaks.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: I like that. Each side owns its part, nobody changes anything alone.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Okay. Decided. I'll write it into the spec tonight. How do we know which version an event is on, though?

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: I'll add a schema version number to every event. So if we ever change something, an old tablet sending old events doesn't confuse anybody. The receiver just reads the number.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Perfect. Okay, last thing. Friday's demo. What do we show Paris?

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: I think exactly what I just showed you. An inspection done offline, then the tablet reconnects and it syncs.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: And then I show the signed PDF for that same inspection. So he sees his first two asks, start to finish.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Love that. And we just say export by site is coming, honestly.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Honestly. Okay. I think we're in good shape. Thanks, Romeo.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Thank you. Say hi to Tybalt. Tell him the clock's running.
